newsitem.title: DENMARK: U.S., Germany push Danish bond prices up.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Germany push Danish bond prices up.

text.p: Danish bond prices climbed in early trade on Wednesday, echoing Wall Street's response to lower than expected U.S. wage costs and shadowing the rising German Bund.
"The American market continued to rise after Danish closing time (on Tuesday), we are following," a dealer said.
At 0730 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 109.68, yielding 6.52 percent, up 0.50 point from Tuesday's close.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 69 basis points from Tuesday's 70 bp.
The crown weakened slightly, to 3.8076 to the mark, from 3.8070.
